scr_close_reports_2.purpose: Runs a single close report on demand at property level — for example re-running the A/R report after a preliminary package showed a variance, exporting it to Excel and sending it to the site team with a specific question about the delinquent or prepaid balance.
scr_close_reports_2.outcome: A focused, property-level report that isolates one reconciliation break and can be handed to the person who can fix it.
scr_close_reports_2.rootCause: Multi-property packages hide which property causes a variance. Running the individual report at property level pinpoints the source, and the Excel export gives the site team something concrete to act on.
scr_close_reports_2.ifSkipped: Variances are escalated vaguely ('A/R doesn't tie'), site teams cannot act, and breaks carry into the next month.
redFlags: Report permission missing (A/R - Multifamily (No Variance) requires specific rights)
Report run for a different period than the package

scr_close_generating_a_report.purpose: Procedure to generate a standard close report by selecting report type, property or group and period — distinct from building a custom financial report in the Financial Reporting module.
scr_close_generating_a_report.outcome: A standard close report output for the selected scope and period.
scr_close_generating_a_report.rootCause: Users confuse close reports (reconciliation-focused) with financial statements; this procedure keeps them in the right tool for tie-outs.
scr_close_generating_a_report.ifSkipped: Users build custom financial reports to do reconciliations, producing inconsistent tie-outs.
redFlags: Tie-outs performed on custom reports that exclude some accounts

scr_close_financial_close_management_rep.purpose: Catalog of the balance-sheet reconciliation reports available in Financial Close Management — cash, A/P, A/R (multifamily, commercial, other), allowance, security deposits, mortgage and escrow, notes payable/receivable, prepaids, accruals, fixed assets, other assets, property tax and rent roll.
scr_close_financial_close_management_rep.outcome: Accountants know which report supports which balance-sheet account in the close package.
scr_close_financial_close_management_rep.rootCause: Every material balance-sheet account needs a reconciliation. Mapping each account group to a standard report ensures coverage of the whole balance sheet.
scr_close_financial_close_management_rep.ifSkipped: Some balance-sheet accounts go unreconciled because nobody knows which report supports them.
redFlags: Balance-sheet accounts with balances but no mapped report

scr_close_cash_and_cash_equivalents_repo.purpose: Explains each column of the Cash & Cash Equivalents report — GL balance, reconciled bank balance, variance, account type — so preparers can read which bank accounts do not tie and why.
scr_close_cash_and_cash_equivalents_repo.outcome: Preparers correctly interpret variances and restricted/unrestricted classification on the cash work paper.
scr_close_cash_and_cash_equivalents_repo.rootCause: Misreading columns (e.g., comparing unreconciled bank balance to GL) leads to false variances or missed real ones.
scr_close_cash_and_cash_equivalents_repo.ifSkipped: Cash variances are misinterpreted and wrongly escalated or ignored.
redFlags: Variance column non-zero on accounts marked reconciled

scr_close_accounts_payable_report.purpose: Compares the vendor aging (A/P subledger) to the 2010 Accounts Payable GL balance at period end and shows payments made, so the preparer can prove the A/P liability on the balance sheet is supported by specific open invoices.
scr_close_accounts_payable_report.outcome: An A/P tie-out work paper showing zero variance, or specific explained reconciling items, between the subledger and GL.
scr_close_accounts_payable_report.rootCause: A/P and GL diverge when JEs are posted directly to the A/P control account, when invoices are posted to a closed summary, or when interfaces fail. The liability owners see must equal the invoices actually owed.
scr_close_accounts_payable_report.ifSkipped: Unsupported A/P balances accumulate, unrecorded liabilities or phantom payables go undetected, and auditors cannot rely on A/P completeness.
redFlags: Non-zero variance between aging and GL
Manual JEs to 2010
Debit balances in the aging

scr_close_accounts_payable_report_column.purpose: Defines the A/P report columns — aging balance per subledger, GL balance, variance and supporting detail — to analyze where a subledger-to-GL difference comes from.
scr_close_accounts_payable_report_column.outcome: Preparers can trace an A/P variance to specific transactions.
scr_close_accounts_payable_report_column.rootCause: Understanding the columns is necessary to separate timing items from true errors.
redFlags: Variances explained as timing without transaction detail

scr_close_a_r_multifamily_report.purpose: Reconciles multifamily resident receivables from OneSite/Accounts Receivable — delinquent balances and prepaid (credit) balances — to the GL A/R and prepaid rent accounts, showing variances by property.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_report.outcome: A resident A/R tie-out that proves 1210 A/R and 2120 Prepaid Rent agree with resident ledgers, including correct gross presentation of prepaids.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_report.rootCause: Resident ledgers live in the property management system while the GL is summarized. Interface timing, manual JEs and miscoded charges cause breaks. GAAP also requires prepaid rent (credit balances) to be shown as a liability rather than netted against receivables.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_report.ifSkipped: Revenue and A/R misstatements persist, prepaid rent is netted into A/R (understating both), and bad-debt reserves are calculated on wrong balances.
gaap: ASC 210-20 — offsetting (prepaids not netted against receivables)
redFlags: Prepaid balances netted into A/R
Variances caused by manual JEs to 1210
Old credit balances for moved-out residents (refund or escheat due)

scr_close_a_r_multifamily_report_columns.purpose: Explains the A/R - Multifamily report's delinquent and prepaid columns versus GL columns, and how variance is computed.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_report_columns.outcome: Preparers correctly separate delinquent and prepaid variances.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_report_columns.rootCause: Delinquent and prepaid balances tie to different GL accounts; confusing them hides real variances.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_report_columns.ifSkipped: Offsetting errors in A/R and prepaids go unnoticed.
redFlags: Net variance zero but delinquent and prepaid variances non-zero

scr_close_a_r_multifamily_no_variance_re.purpose: Variant of the multifamily A/R report that lists receivable balances without calculating variance to the GL — used when the reviewer only needs the balance detail, or when the GL uses a different account structure.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_no_variance_re.outcome: A clean listing of resident receivables and prepaids for the package or for owner requests.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_no_variance_re.rootCause: Some owners' charts of accounts do not map one-to-one to the report's variance logic, producing false variances; the no-variance version provides the detail without misleading comparisons.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_no_variance_re.ifSkipped: False variances confuse reviewers, or detail is unavailable for owners.
redFlags: Using the no-variance report to avoid showing a real variance

scr_close_a_r_multifamily_no_variance_re.purpose: Defines the columns of the no-variance multifamily A/R report — resident, unit, delinquent balance, prepaid balance, aging.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_no_variance_re.outcome: Correct interpretation of receivable detail without GL comparison.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_no_variance_re.rootCause: Reviewers need to know the report omits the GL comparison so they perform the tie-out separately.
scr_close_a_r_multifamily_no_variance_re.ifSkipped: Reviewers assume a tie-out was performed when it was not.
redFlags: No separate GL tie-out when this report is used

scr_close_allowance_for_doubtful_account.purpose: Shows the estimated uncollectible portion of receivables — typically reserved by aging bucket (e.g., 100% of former-resident balances, 50% of 60+ days) — and compares it to the 1215 Allowance balance so the reserve can be adjusted at month-end.
scr_close_allowance_for_doubtful_account.outcome: A supported bad-debt reserve and the monthly adjusting entry (DR 4050 Bad Debt / CR 1215 Allowance) that keeps receivables at net realizable value.
scr_close_allowance_for_doubtful_account.rootCause: Rent receivables from delinquent and moved-out residents are frequently uncollectible. Reporting them at face value overstates assets and revenue. Owners also track bad debt as a percentage of revenue as a key operating metric.
scr_close_allowance_for_doubtful_account.ifSkipped: A/R is overstated, bad debt is recognized in large lumps at write-off, and revenue quality is misrepresented.
gaap: ASC 842-30-25-12 — lease income when collectibility is not probable
redFlags: Allowance not changing while aging deteriorates
Former-resident balances not fully reserved
Allowance exceeding total receivables

scr_close_allowance_for_doubtful_account.purpose: Explains the allowance report columns — balance per aging bucket, reserve percentage per bucket, calculated reserve, current 1215 Allowance balance and the adjustment needed — so the preparer can book the month's bad-debt entry.
scr_close_allowance_for_doubtful_account.outcome: A calculated reserve adjustment (DR 4050 Bad Debt / CR 1215 Allowance, or the reverse) supported bucket by bucket.
scr_close_allowance_for_doubtful_account.rootCause: The reserve method (e.g., 25% of 31-60, 50% of 61-90, 100% of 90+ and former residents) must be applied consistently each month. The columns make the method transparent so reviewers can verify it instead of accepting a single number.
scr_close_allowance_for_doubtful_account.ifSkipped: Reserve adjustments are booked as plugs, bad debt swings unpredictably, and auditors challenge the estimate's consistency.
redFlags: Reserve percentages changed from last month without documented approval
Calculated reserve differing from the booked allowance after the adjustment

scr_close_a_r_commercial_report.purpose: Reconciles commercial tenant receivables — base rent, CAM, real estate tax and insurance recoveries, percentage rent — from the Accounts Receivable subledger to the GL for retail or office components of a property.
scr_close_a_r_commercial_report.outcome: A commercial A/R tie-out that supports tenant receivables, including recovery billings and straight-line rent where tracked.
scr_close_a_r_commercial_report.rootCause: Mixed-use multifamily properties often include ground-floor retail. Commercial leases have complex billing (CAM estimates, year-end reconciliations) that frequently diverges from the GL.
scr_close_a_r_commercial_report.ifSkipped: Commercial receivables and recovery income are misstated, and CAM reconciliation disputes with tenants escalate.
gaap: ASC 842-30 — lessor accounting including straight-line rent
redFlags: CAM estimate billings not trued up annually
Straight-line receivable not reconciled

scr_close_a_r_commercial_report_columns.purpose: Defines each column of the commercial A/R reconciliation — tenant, charge type (base rent, CAM, tax and insurance recovery, percentage rent), subledger balance, GL balance and variance — so the preparer can trace a commercial receivable break to a specific tenant and charge code.
scr_close_a_r_commercial_report_columns.outcome: A commercial A/R variance is pinned to one tenant and one charge type, e.g. a CAM estimate billed in A/R but posted to the wrong recovery income account.
scr_close_a_r_commercial_report_columns.rootCause: Commercial leases generate many charge codes that map to different GL recovery accounts. A variance that nets to zero across charge types can still hide offsetting errors (CAM billed to tax recovery). Reading the columns by charge type is the only way to see them.
scr_close_a_r_commercial_report_columns.ifSkipped: Offsetting charge-code errors survive the tie-out, and year-end CAM reconciliations to tenants start from wrong recovery balances, leading to tenant disputes and refunds.
redFlags: Net variance zero but individual charge-type variances non-zero
Tenants with recovery billings but no lease abstract support

scr_close_a_r_other_report.purpose: Reconciles non-resident receivables from the Accounts Receivable customer aging — affiliates, insurance claims receivable, utility company rebates, vendors owing refunds, ancillary contract partners — to the GL.
scr_close_a_r_other_report.outcome: Other receivables are supported and aged, and stale items are identified for collection or write-off.
scr_close_a_r_other_report.rootCause: Miscellaneous receivables are often forgotten after being recorded (e.g., an insurance claim receivable after a casualty). Periodic reconciliation keeps them collectible and supported.
scr_close_a_r_other_report.ifSkipped: Stale receivables stay on the balance sheet, overstating assets.
gaap: ASC 326 — credit losses on other receivables
redFlags: Receivables older than one year without collection activity

scr_close_a_r_other_report_columns.purpose: Explains how the A/R - Other report lines up each non-resident customer's aging balance (affiliates, insurance carriers, utility rebates, vendor refunds) against the GL accounts those receivables post to, and how the variance is computed.
scr_close_a_r_other_report_columns.outcome: Preparers can match each miscellaneous receivable to its GL account and identify which customer causes a break.
scr_close_a_r_other_report_columns.rootCause: Other receivables are spread across several GL accounts (Due From Affiliates, insurance claims receivable, other receivables). Without understanding which columns map to which accounts, preparers compare the wrong totals and report false variances.
scr_close_a_r_other_report_columns.ifSkipped: False variances waste reviewer time, or real breaks (a receivable posted to the wrong account) are missed.
redFlags: Receivables in the aging mapped to an account outside the report's account group
Customers with credit balances left in other receivables

scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.purpose: Reconciles resident security deposits held per OneSite resident ledgers to the 2110 Resident Security Deposits GL balance, with variance by property.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.outcome: A deposit liability tie-out supporting both the balance sheet and state trust-account compliance.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.rootCause: Deposits collected at move-in and dispositioned at move-out flow through the property management system; posting and interface errors cause the GL to drift from what residents are actually owed.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.ifSkipped: Deposit liabilities are misstated, refunds may be wrong, and trust-account shortfalls go unnoticed.
redFlags: Variance between resident deposits and 2110
Deposits for former residents past the statutory refund deadline

scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.purpose: Defines the multifamily deposit report columns — deposits held per resident ledger by type (security, pet, key/amenity), GL balance and variance — so the preparer can isolate which deposit type causes a break.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.outcome: A deposit variance is traced to a deposit type, often pet deposits posted to income or key deposits posted to a different liability account.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.rootCause: Deposit types frequently map to different GL accounts, and pet fees (non-refundable, income) are often confused with pet deposits (refundable, liability). The column breakdown exposes those misclassifications.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.ifSkipped: Refundable deposits are recorded as income, understating liabilities and exposing the owner to statutory penalties at move-out.
gaap: ASC 606 — non-refundable fees vs refundable deposits
redFlags: Pet deposits recorded in income
Variance concentrated in one deposit type

scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.purpose: Lists multifamily security deposits held by resident without comparing to the GL, used for resident-level detail or when the chart of accounts does not map cleanly to the variance logic.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.outcome: Resident-level deposit detail for the package or compliance review.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.rootCause: Compliance reviews and owner requests often need resident-level deposit listings independent of the GL comparison.
redFlags: No separate GL tie-out when using this report

scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.purpose: Explains the columns of the no-variance deposit listing — resident, unit, move-in date, deposit types and amounts held — which lists deposits without comparing them to the GL.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.outcome: Reviewers understand that this report is a listing only, and that the 2110 tie-out must be done separately.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.rootCause: Because this variant omits the GL comparison, reviewers can mistake it for a completed tie-out. Knowing the columns prevents that assumption.
scr_close_security_deposits_multifamily_.ifSkipped: Packages go out with a deposit listing but no actual reconciliation to 2110, and a deposit shortfall is missed.
redFlags: Package includes only the no-variance listing with no separate tie-out

scr_close_security_deposits_commercial_r.purpose: Reconciles commercial tenant security deposits (including letters of credit tracked off-balance-sheet) to the GL deposit liability.
scr_close_security_deposits_commercial_r.outcome: Commercial deposit liabilities are supported by tenant-level detail.
scr_close_security_deposits_commercial_r.rootCause: Commercial deposits are larger and governed by lease terms; errors affect tenant relationships and lease compliance.
redFlags: Letters of credit recorded as cash deposits

scr_close_security_deposits_commercial_r.purpose: Defines the commercial security deposit columns — tenant, lease, deposit required per lease, deposit held, GL balance and variance — used to reconcile commercial tenant deposits.
scr_close_security_deposits_commercial_r.outcome: Commercial deposit balances are matched to lease requirements and the GL, tenant by tenant.
scr_close_security_deposits_commercial_r.rootCause: Commercial leases specify deposit amounts, and some tenants provide letters of credit instead of cash. Comparing held versus required, and cash versus GL, catches missing deposits and LCs wrongly recorded as cash.
scr_close_security_deposits_commercial_r.ifSkipped: Deposit shortfalls against lease terms go unnoticed, and letters of credit may be booked as cash liabilities.
redFlags: Deposit held less than the lease requirement
Letters of credit recorded in the GL as cash deposits

scr_close_mortgage_and_escrow_report_col.purpose: Explains how the mortgage and escrow report shows the monthly payment split — principal, interest, tax escrow, insurance escrow, reserve deposits — and escrow disbursements.
scr_close_mortgage_and_escrow_report_col.outcome: Preparers correctly map each component to the right GL account.
scr_close_mortgage_and_escrow_report_col.rootCause: Misreading the payment split sends principal to interest or escrow deposits to expense.
scr_close_mortgage_and_escrow_report_col.ifSkipped: Debt and escrow balances drift from servicer records.
redFlags: Escrow deposits expensed

scr_close_notes_payable_report.purpose: Details formal debt obligations — mortgage loans, mezzanine loans, seller financing, affiliate notes — with principal balances, rates and maturity, and ties them to the GL.
scr_close_notes_payable_report.outcome: A debt schedule supporting the balance sheet and lender covenant reporting, including current vs long-term classification.
scr_close_notes_payable_report.rootCause: Debt is often the largest liability. Owners, lenders and auditors require a schedule tying outstanding principal to lender statements, and maturities drive refinancing decisions.
scr_close_notes_payable_report.ifSkipped: Debt balances are unsupported, maturities are missed, and covenant reporting is inaccurate.
redFlags: Principal per GL differs from lender statement
Debt maturing within 12 months not flagged

scr_close_notes_payable_report_columns.purpose: Defines the notes payable columns — lender, original principal, current principal, interest rate (fixed or floating with index and spread), payment schedule and maturity date — used to build the debt schedule and classify the current portion.
scr_close_notes_payable_report_columns.outcome: A debt schedule where each loan's balance, rate and maturity can be checked against the loan documents and servicer statement.
scr_close_notes_payable_report_columns.rootCause: Maturity and payment-schedule columns determine current vs long-term classification and flag refinancing risk. Floating-rate loans also require the rate column to reconcile interest expense and any interest rate cap or swap.
scr_close_notes_payable_report_columns.ifSkipped: Debt maturing within 12 months is misclassified as long-term, and interest expense on floating-rate loans is not reconciled to the index.
gaap: ASC 815 — interest rate caps and swaps on floating-rate debt
redFlags: Maturity within 12 months not highlighted
Floating rate not updated for the current index reset

scr_close_notes_receivable_report.purpose: Details promissory notes owed to the entity — seller notes from a property sale, loans to affiliates or partners, resident payment plans formalized as notes — with balances and collection status.
scr_close_notes_receivable_report.outcome: Notes receivable are supported, aged and assessed for collectibility.
scr_close_notes_receivable_report.rootCause: Notes receivable carry credit risk and often involve related parties, which require disclosure and scrutiny.
scr_close_notes_receivable_report.ifSkipped: Uncollectible notes remain at face value, and related-party balances go undisclosed.
redFlags: Notes with no payments received
Related-party notes without documentation

scr_close_notes_receivable_report_column.purpose: Defines the notes receivable columns — borrower, principal, interest rate, payment schedule, due date and balance — for loans owed to the entity, such as seller financing on a disposition or a loan to an affiliate.
scr_close_notes_receivable_report_column.outcome: Each note can be verified against the note agreement and assessed for collectibility and classification.
scr_close_notes_receivable_report_column.rootCause: Notes receivable often involve related parties or buyers of sold properties. Due dates drive current vs long-term classification, and missed scheduled payments are the first signal of impairment.
scr_close_notes_receivable_report_column.ifSkipped: Past-due notes go unreserved and related-party notes are not disclosed.
redFlags: Scheduled payments not received
Interest accrued but never collected

scr_close_prepaid_expense_report_columns.purpose: Explains the prepaid report columns — item, original amount, term, monthly amortization, amortized to date, remaining balance and GL comparison — for each insurance, tax, license or contract prepayment.
scr_close_prepaid_expense_report_columns.outcome: Preparers verify that each prepaid is amortizing at the right rate and that the remaining balances sum to 1310.
scr_close_prepaid_expense_report_columns.rootCause: Prepaid errors are visible only at item level: a 12-month schedule on a 13-month policy, a cancelled policy still amortizing, a renewal never set up. The columns make each item's math checkable.
scr_close_prepaid_expense_report_columns.ifSkipped: Item-level amortization errors go unnoticed and 1310 carries expired or unscheduled balances.
redFlags: Remaining balance on items past their end date
Monthly amortization not equal to original amount ÷ term

scr_close_accrued_expenses_report_column.purpose: Defines the accrued expenses report columns — vendor, GL account, accrual period, amount, reversal status and GL comparison — so preparers can separate current-month accruals from stale ones that failed to reverse.
scr_close_accrued_expenses_report_column.outcome: Every line in 2020 Accrued Expenses is classified as current, awaiting reversal, or stale and needing correction.
scr_close_accrued_expenses_report_column.rootCause: The reversal-status and period columns are what reveal accrual hygiene problems: an accrual from three months ago still sitting in 2020 means either the reversal failed or the actual invoice was coded elsewhere, double-counting expense.
scr_close_accrued_expenses_report_column.ifSkipped: Stale accruals accumulate in 2020 Accrued Expenses, overstating liabilities and expenses, and auditors flag unsupported accrued balances.
redFlags: Accrual periods older than 60 days
Reversal status 'not reversed' for prior-month auto-reversing entries

scr_close_fixed_assets_report.purpose: Summarizes fixed asset balances — cost by class, accumulated depreciation, net book value, additions and disposals for the period — for the close package, tied to GL asset accounts.
scr_close_fixed_assets_report.outcome: A fixed asset roll-forward work paper supporting the largest balance on the balance sheet.
scr_close_fixed_assets_report.rootCause: Fixed assets change through capital projects and disposals every month in value-add portfolios. A monthly roll-forward catches capital spend not capitalized and disposals not recorded.
scr_close_fixed_assets_report.ifSkipped: Fixed asset balances drift from the register and year-end requires large corrections.
redFlags: Additions in the GL with no register additions
Negative net book values

scr_close_fixed_assets_report_columns.purpose: Explains the fixed assets report roll-forward columns — beginning cost, additions, disposals, ending cost, beginning accumulated depreciation, depreciation for the period, accumulated depreciation on disposals, ending net book value — by asset class.
scr_close_fixed_assets_report_columns.outcome: Preparers can see which component of the roll-forward is missing, e.g. additions in the GL with no matching additions column, or disposals without accumulated depreciation removed.
scr_close_fixed_assets_report_columns.rootCause: Fixed asset errors show up as a roll-forward that does not foot: capital invoices coded to 1530 without an asset record, or a disposal that removed cost but not accumulated depreciation. The columns are the diagnostic tool.
scr_close_fixed_assets_report_columns.ifSkipped: Roll-forward breaks are not diagnosed and the register drifts further from the GL each month.
redFlags: Disposals column populated for cost but not for accumulated depreciation
Depreciation column not equal to the posted depreciation entry

scr_close_other_assets_report.purpose: Reconciles miscellaneous assets that do not fit standard categories — utility deposits held by utility companies, deferred leasing costs, deferred financing costs, deposits on purchases — using a selected GL account group.
scr_close_other_assets_report.outcome: Miscellaneous asset balances are supported and reviewed for impairment or write-off.
scr_close_other_assets_report.rootCause: Other assets are often recorded once and forgotten (e.g., a utility deposit refunded years ago but never cleared). A periodic review prevents stale balances.
scr_close_other_assets_report.ifSkipped: Stale or unsupported other-asset balances persist.
gaap: ASC 340 — other assets and deferred costs
redFlags: Other-asset balances unchanged for years

scr_close_other_assets_report_columns.purpose: Defines the columns of the Other Assets report — GL account within the selected account group, balance, and comparison — for miscellaneous assets such as utility deposits, deferred leasing commissions and deferred financing costs.
scr_close_other_assets_report_columns.outcome: Preparers know which accounts the report covered and can tie each miscellaneous asset balance to its support.
scr_close_other_assets_report_columns.rootCause: The report only covers the G/L account group selected; accounts outside it are silently excluded. Knowing the columns and the group scope prevents a false conclusion that all other assets were reconciled.
scr_close_other_assets_report_columns.ifSkipped: Other-asset accounts outside the selected group go unreconciled for months.
redFlags: Other-asset accounts with balances not in the selected account group

scr_close_property_tax_report.purpose: Tracks property tax assessments, liability, installments and payments — including jurisdictions that bill in arrears versus in advance — to support the real estate tax accrual or prepaid at period end.
scr_close_property_tax_report.outcome: A supported real estate tax accrual or prepaid balance and correct monthly tax expense.
scr_close_property_tax_report.rootCause: Real estate taxes are often the largest operating expense. Billing cycles vary by jurisdiction (Texas bills in arrears annually; others in advance semi-annually). Monthly expense must be accrued evenly regardless of payment timing.
scr_close_property_tax_report.ifSkipped: Tax expense swings with payment timing, accruals are unsupported, and reassessment increases are not reflected.
gaap: ASC 720-30 — real and personal property taxes
redFlags: Accrual based on prior-year tax without adjusting for reassessment
Taxes paid from escrow not recorded

scr_close_property_tax_report_columns.purpose: Explains the property tax columns — assessed value, tax rate, annual liability, installments paid, accrued or prepaid balance — so the preparer can confirm the month's tax expense and the balance-sheet position.
scr_close_property_tax_report_columns.outcome: A tax accrual or prepaid balance supported by the assessment and payment history.
scr_close_property_tax_report_columns.rootCause: Whether the property needs an accrual or a prepaid depends on the jurisdiction's billing cycle (arrears vs advance). The liability and paid columns show which applies and how large it should be.
scr_close_property_tax_report_columns.ifSkipped: Accruals and prepaids are set on the wrong side of the balance sheet, and reassessment increases are missed until the bill arrives.
gaap: ASC 720-30 — real and personal property taxes
redFlags: Annual liability based on the prior-year assessment after a reassessment notice
Paid column not matching servicer escrow disbursements

scr_close_rent_roll_report.purpose: Includes the rent roll in the close package — each unit with tenant, lease terms, rent, payment status — to support the revenue and occupancy figures in the owner financials.
scr_close_rent_roll_report.outcome: Rent roll evidence in the package for GPR and occupancy tie-outs.
scr_close_rent_roll_report.rootCause: Revenue reported to owners must be supported by the rent roll as of month-end; including it in the package freezes the month-end snapshot.
scr_close_rent_roll_report.ifSkipped: Revenue support is missing from close evidence.
redFlags: Rent roll dated after month-end

scr_close_rent_roll_report_columns.purpose: Defines the rent roll columns — unit, unit type, resident, lease start and end, market rent, lease rent, concessions, balance and status — used in the close package to support revenue and occupancy.
scr_close_rent_roll_report_columns.outcome: Preparers can compute GPR (sum of market rent), loss to lease (market minus lease rent) and vacancy from the rent roll to tie to the GL.
scr_close_rent_roll_report_columns.rootCause: The GPR tie-out relies on reading market rent versus lease rent correctly. Confusing the two columns misstates loss to lease, one of the metrics asset managers use to judge pricing.
scr_close_rent_roll_report_columns.ifSkipped: Loss-to-lease and vacancy loss are miscalculated, and revenue components in the owner package do not tie to the rent roll.
redFlags: Market rent blank or zero for vacant units
Lease rent above market rent without explanation (gain to lease)
